narrative:
The model estimates a 64% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest influence pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while many had 6 or more years. This lack of broader career history appears to have signaled higher turnover risk to the system.

The fact that you have received other job offers while at the company was the second most important factor, and it pushed the prediction strongly toward leaving. Most employees the model predicted would stay had not received outside opportunities.

Your employment in the "other" sector, rather than medical or education, was the third notable influence and also nudged the outcome toward leaving. Only about 22% of employees predicted to stay work in this category.

While some positive signals exist, such as your medium level of emotional commitment and job engagement, they were not strong enough to outweigh the top factors. The organization should consider discussing your career development goals with you and exploring ways to increase your sense of stability and recognition. You may want to reflect on whether the external opportunities better align with your long-term plans. (248 words)
